definitions.explanation: A movie produced outside Japan, especially from Western countries. Used to categorize films in movie listings, rental shops, and streaming services.
Painting done in Western techniques (oil painting, watercolor, etc.) as opposed to traditional Japanese-style painting.

examples.japanese: {洋画|ようが}は{字幕|じまく}で{見|み}る{派|は}だ。
examples.english: I'm the type who watches foreign movies with subtitles.

examples.japanese: {洋画|ようが}の{吹|ふ}き{替|か}えは{声優|せいゆう}がうまいと{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: Dubbed foreign movies are enjoyable when the voice actors are good.

examples.japanese: この{配信|はいしん}サービスは{邦画|ほうが}より{洋画|ようが}のラインナップが{充実|じゅうじつ}している。
examples.english: This streaming service has a better selection of foreign films than Japanese ones.

examples.japanese: {美術館|びじゅつかん}で{洋画|ようが}の{展覧会|てんらんかい}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw a Western painting exhibition at the art museum.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{多|おお}くの{画家|がか}がヨーロッパで{洋画|ようが}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, many painters studied Western painting in Europe.

examples.japanese: {日本画|にほんが}と{洋画|ようが}の{技法|ぎほう}を{融合|ゆうごう}させた{作品|さくひん}が{注目|ちゅうもく}されている。
examples.english: Works that fuse Japanese and Western painting techniques are attracting attention.

notes:
Has two distinct meanings depending on context.

SENSE 1 (film):
Contrasts with {邦画|ほうが} (Japanese film). In practice, {洋画|ようが} covers all non-Japanese films, not just Western ones, though the label originated from that distinction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (film):
- {洋画|ようが}の{字幕|じまく} (subtitles for a foreign film)
- {洋画|ようが}の{吹|ふ}き{替|か}え (dubbed foreign film)

SENSE 2 (painting):
Contrasts with {日本画|にほんが} (Japanese-style painting). Refers to Western art techniques like oil painting ({油絵|あぶらえ}) and watercolor ({水彩画|すいさいが}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (painting):
- {洋画家|ようがか} (Western-style painter)
- {洋画|ようが}の{技法|ぎほう} (Western painting techniques)
